issue: Does 8 U.S.C. § 1225(b)(2)(A) mandatorily detain noncitizens who entered without inspection and have lived in the United States for years, or does § 1226 govern them and entitle them to a bond hearing?

sides.position: Section 1226 applies to noncitizens present in the United States for years regardless of how they entered, so they are entitled to a bond hearing and are not subject to mandatory detention under Section 1225.

sides.position: Section 1225 applies to all noncitizens who have not been admitted to the United States, so they must be detained without bond.

this_court: Section 1226 applies to these petitioners, so they are entitled to a bond hearing (the Fourth Circuit joins the majority position).
quote: The debate has now reached every numbered United States court of appeals and has led to a circuit split.
